## remarkable
# reMarkable MCP Server

Access documents from your reMarkable tablet. All operations are read-only.

## Available Tools

- `remarkable_browse(path, query)` - Browse folders or search for documents
- `remarkable_read(document, content_type, page, grep)` - Read document content with pagination
- `remarkable_recent(limit)` - Get recently modified documents
- `remarkable_status()` - Check connection and diagnose issues
- `remarkable_image(document, page, include_ocr)` - Get a PNG image with optional OCR

## Recommended Workflows

### Finding and Reading Documents
1. Use `remarkable_browse(query="keyword")` to search by name
2. Use `remarkable_read("Document Name")` to get content
3. Use `remarkable_read("Document", page=2)` to continue reading long documents
4. Use `remarkable_read("Document", grep="pattern")` to search within a document

### Getting Page Images
Use `remarkable_image` when you need visual context:
- Hand-drawn diagrams, sketches, or UI mockups
- Content that text extraction might miss
- Implementing designs based on hand-drawn wireframes

Example: `remarkable_image("UI Mockup", page=1)` returns a PNG image
Example: `remarkable_image("Notes", include_ocr=True)` returns image with extracted text

### For Large Documents
Use pagination to avoid overwhelming context. The response includes:
- `page` / `total_pages` - current position
- `more` - true if more content exists
- `next_page` - page number to request next

### Combining Tools
- Browse → Read: Find documents first, then read them
- Recent → Read: Check what was recently modified, then read specific ones
- Read with grep: Search for specific content within large documents
- Browse → Image: Find a document then get its visual representation

## MCP Resources

Documents are registered as resources for direct access:
- `remarkable:///{path}.txt` - Get full extracted text content in one request
- `remarkableimg:///{path}.page-{N}.png` - Get PNG image of page N (notebooks only)
- Use resources when you need complete document content without pagination… [truncated]

===== Proulx_PFD_Decision_Letter.docx
Baylor Athletics Innovation and Research
Steering Committee
[Date]
Dr. Laurel Proulx
Baylor Pelvic Health and Rehabilitation Research Lab
Baylor University

cc: Dr. Mandy Parra, Tarleton State University

Re: Identification of Sport Specific Movement and Lifestyle Risk Factors for Pelvic Floor Dysfunction in Female Athletes (Baylor IRB #2373733)

Dear Dr. Proulx,
The BAIR Steering Committee has completed its review of your request to recruit Baylor student-athletes for the study referenced above.
Decision: Approved, subject to the conditions listed below.
The committee scored the proposal 75 out of 100, which places it in the High Priority tier. That reflects several things at once. The work addresses a condition that affects a large share of female athletes and that the existing risk models do not explain. It is led out of a Baylor lab, which means the resulting body of work builds Baylor's reputation rather than someone else's. Your IRB approval, validated instruments, and 500-participant target mean the science was not in question. And the burden on athletes is a voluntary survey they complete on their own time, with the in-person portion optional and off campus.
The committee also noted that this opens a research area the department currently has no presence in, and that it serves a population the framework was specifically written to encourage.

Conditions of approval
These concern how the study reaches Baylor athletes, not the protocol itself. None require changes to your IRB-approved design. Recruitment of Baylor athletes should not begin until items 1 through 5 are settled.
Recruitment channel. Your submission says Baylor athletes will be recruited via athletics department promotion. Before any material goes out, we need agreement in writing on the channel. Recruitment cannot run through head coaches, position coaches, or strength and conditioning staff. Distribution through Sports Medicine, a student-athlete development email, an athlete portal, or flyers posted in spaces athletes access privately all work. This is a standing requirement in our framework: student-athletes are treated as a population at risk of coercion because of the influence coaching and support staff hold over playing time, so recruitment has to happen away from them.
Athlete preparation. Our framework asks that studies touching reproductive health include background education and preparation for participants. Athletes should know what the survey covers before they open it, and should understand that whether they take it is not visible to anyone in the athletics department.
Referral pathway. A screening survey of this kind will identify athletes with symptoms. Sports Medicine will designate a clinical contact, and we would like the survey materials to tell participants where to go if they want follow-up care.
Incentive raffle. The $50 gift card drawing needs a determination from NCAA compliance before recruitment starts. Research participation incentives are usually permissible, but because the drawing is offered to athletes rather than to the general student body, compliance has to make the call rather than us. Eric Rash will route this.
Data use agreement. Section 3.2 states that all data remains solely Baylor property, while Phase 2 measurements will be collected on Tarleton State equipment. Please execute a written data use agreement covering that arrangement.
Sports in scope and timing. Confirm which Baylor programs you intend to recruit from so we can time distribution away from championship windows and finals.
IRB status report. Your report is due October 30, 2026, which falls inside your recruitment window. Please keep us copied when it is filed so our records stay current.

Liaison and next steps
Eric Rash will serve as your committee liaison. He will connect you with Sports Medicine on items 2 and 3, route the compliance question in item 4, and confirm the recruitment channel in item 1. Please reach out to him directly to get those moving. The committee recognizes the timing pressure, since your IRB has been in place since November and Phase 1 recruitment is already underway elsewhere. These items can be worked in parallel.
A letter of support on Baylor letterhead is available for grant applications, including the Department of Defense submission your timeline anticipates. Let Eric know when you need it and what it should reference.
The committee is glad to see this work and would welcome a briefing on Phase 1 findings when you reach the analysis stage.
Sincerely,

Eric Rash
On behalf of the BAIR Steering Committee
Baylor Athletics Innovation and Research

# DOCX creation, editing, and analysis

A `.docx` is a ZIP archive of XML files. Choose your approach by task:

| Task | Approach |
|---|---|
| **Create** a new document | Write a `docx` (npm) script — see gotchas below |
| **Edit** an existing document | `unzip` → edit `word/document.xml` → `zip` (docx-js cannot open existing files) |
| **Read** content | `pandoc -t markdown file.docx` |

> Script paths below are relative to this skill's directory.

## Creating with docx-js — gotchas

`docx` is preinstalled — do not run `npm install` first; write the script and `require('docx')` directly. Only if that require fails: `npm install docx`. The model knows the API; these are the footguns:

- **Page size defaults to A4.** For US Letter set `page: { size: { width: 12240, height: 15840 } }` (DXA; 1440 = 1″).
- **Landscape:** pass portrait dimensions and `orientation: PageOrientation.LANDSCAPE` — docx-js swaps width/height internally.
- **Tables need dual widths:** set `columnWidths` on the table AND `width` on every cell, both in `WidthType.DXA` (PERCENTAGE breaks in Google Docs). Column widths must sum to the table width.
- **Table shading:** use `ShadingType.CLEAR`, never `SOLID` (renders black).
- **Lists:** never insert `•` literally; use a `numbering` config with `LevelFormat.BULLET`.
- **`ImageRun` requires `type:`** (`"png"`, `"jpg"`, …).
- **`PageBreak` must be inside a `Paragraph`.**
- **Never use `\n`** — use separate `Paragraph` elements.
- **TOC:** headings must use built-in `HeadingLevel.*`; custom heading styles need `outlineLevel` set or they won't appear.
- **Don't use a table as a horizontal rule** — use a paragraph bottom border instead.
- **Dot-leader / right-aligned-on-same-line:** use `PositionalTab` (`alignment: PositionalTabAlignment.RIGHT`, `leader: PositionalTabLeader.DOT`) inside a `TextRun`, not literal `.` or space padding.

## Verify the output

After writing a `.docx`, render it and look at it:

```bash
python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to pdf output.docx
pdftoppm -jpeg -r 100 output.pdf page
ls page-*.jpg   # then Read the images
```

`pdftoppm` zero-pads page numbers to the width of the page count (`page-01.jpg`…`page-12.jpg`).

## Editing existing documents

Legacy `.doc` files must be converted first: `python scripts/office/soffice.py --headless --convert-to docx file.doc`.

```bash
unzip -q doc.docx -d unpacked/
find unpacked -type l -delete   # strip symlink entries — docx from external parties is untrusted
python scripts/merge_runs.py unpacked/   # coalesce fragmented runs so text is findable
# edit unpacked/word/document.xml in place — do NOT reformat or pretty-print
(cd unpacked && rm -f ../out.docx && zip -Xr ../out.docx .)
python scripts/office/validate.py out.docx --original doc.docx   # XSD checks; --auto-repair fixes common issues
# redlining? add --author "<the name you redlined under>" to check every edit is tracked
```

Word splits text across many `<w:r>` runs (revision ids, spell-check markers), so a phrase you can see in the document often doesn't exist as a contiguous string in the XML. `merge_runs.py` merges adjacent identically-formatted runs in `word/document.xml` without changing content or rendering; it also accepts a `.docx` directly (`python scripts/merge_runs.py doc.docx -o merged.docx`).

**Tracked changes:** when redlining, validate with `--author "<the name you redlined under>"` (needs `--original`) — it reports any text you changed without a `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` around it, which is easy to do by accident and invisible in the accepted view. Wrap runs in `<w:ins>`/`<w:del>` with `w:id`, `w:author`, `w:date` attributes. Inside `<w:del>`, the text element is `<w:delText>`, not `<w:t>`. A deleted paragraph mark (`<w:pPr><w:rPr><w:del w:id=".." w:author=".." w:date=".."/></w:rPr></w:pPr>`) means "merge this paragraph into the next" — so deleting a paragraph outright is that plus a `<w:del>` around every run. The `<w:del/>` must come before the rPr's other children; their order is schema-enforced.

To produce a clean copy with all tracked changes accepted: `python scripts/accept_changes.py in.docx out.docx`.

Accepting a deleted paragraph mark should join that paragraph to the one below it, so a paragraph whose runs are *all* deleted vanishes. Word does this; `accept_changes.py` and `pandoc --track-changes=accept` don't always. Both fail the same way — they strip the deleted text but leave the emptied paragraph behind, which reads as a stray empty bullet when it was auto-numbered:

- `pandoc --track-changes=accept` never joins the paragraphs.
- `accept_changes.py` (LibreOffice) joins them correctly, except when the deleted paragraph is followed by an empty spacer paragraph.

An empty bullet in either view is an artifact of that view, not a defect in the document. Check paragraph deletions in the XML.

## Comments

Comments require six cross-linked files. Use the helper — directory mode when you'll also be editing `document.xml` (saves an unzip/rezip cycle), `.docx`-direct mode otherwise:

```bash
# Against an already-unpacked directory (preferred when also placing markers)
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Fees & expenses cap is too low"
python scripts/comment.py unpacked/ "Agreed" --parent 0

# Against a .docx directly
python scripts/comment.py contract.docx "This cap is too low" -o annotated.docx
```

The script writes `comments.xml`, `commentsExtended.xml`, `commentsIds.xml`, `commentsExtensible.xml`, the relationships, and the content-type overrides. Comment IDs are auto-assigned. It then prints the `<w:commentRangeStart>`/`<w:commentRangeEnd>`/`<w:commentReference>` snippet to add to `word/document.xml` so the comment anchors to specific text — until you place those markers, the comment exists but is not visible.

## Dependencies

`docx` (npm, preinstalled — install only if `require('docx')` fails) · `pandoc` · LibreOffice (`soffice`) · `pdftoppm` (Poppler)

**Subject:** BAIR approval: Pelvic floor dysfunction study (IRB #2373733)

Dr. Proulx,

The BAIR Steering Committee has approved your request to recruit Baylor student-athletes for your pelvic floor dysfunction study. The decision letter and evaluation summary are attached.

The approval covers Phase 1, the online survey, only. That matches your plan to use Baylor for Phase 1. Baylor athletes won't be recruited into Phase 2, so the survey link and materials they receive shouldn't include the Phase 2 opt-in.

A few conditions need to be settled before recruitment starts. They're all about how the survey reaches our athletes, not about your protocol. The ones I'll help move forward:

- **Recruitment channel.** We'll agree on it in writing. It can't go through coaches or Athletic Performance staff.
- **Athlete preparation and referral.** I'll connect you with Athletic Medicine to set up both.
- **Gift card raffle.** I'll send this to NCAA compliance.
- **Data use agreement with Tarleton.** It's only needed if Tarleton will see Baylor athletes' survey responses. If they won't, a short written confirmation closes this item.

Could you also send me the Baylor sports you'd like to include? That lets us plan distribution around championship windows and finals.

If a letter of support would help with the DoD submission, just let me know.

Looking forward to working with you on this.

Eric Rash
Director of Applied Performance, Baylor Athletics
On behalf of the BAIR Steering Committee

---

Attach the two PDFs:
- 2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Decision_Letter_Phase1.pdf
- 2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Eval_Report_Phase1.pdf

import docx, shutil, re, zipfile, os
from xml.sax.saxutils import escape
D = r"G:/My Drive/00_Primary_Storage_Drive/04_RESEARCH/02_Proposals/Approved/2026-08-20_Proulx_PelvicFloor_FemaleAthletes/"
src = docx.Document(D + "2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Decision_Letter_Phase1.docx")
T = [p.text for p in src.paragraphs]
get = lambda s: next(t for t in T if t.startswith(s))

GREEN = '<w:color w:val="1E6B33"/>'
def run(text, b=False, extra=''):
    rpr = ('<w:b/><w:bCs/>' if b else '') + extra
    rpr = f'<w:rPr>{rpr}</w:rPr>' if rpr else ''
    return f'<w:r>{rpr}<w:t xml:space="preserve">{escape(text)}</w:t></w:r>'
def para(runs, before=0, after=80, jc=None, num=None):
    ppr = ''
    if num: ppr += f'<w:pStyle w:val="ListParagraph"/><w:numPr><w:ilvl w:val="0"/><w:numId w:val="{num}"/></w:numPr>'
    ppr += f'<w:spacing w:before="{before}" w:after="{after}"/>'
    if jc: ppr += f'<w:jc w:val="{jc}"/>'
    return f'<w:p><w:pPr>{ppr}</w:pPr>{"".join(runs)}</w:p>'
def lead(t):  # "Label. rest" -> bold label
    i = t.index('. ') + 1 if not t.startswith('Scope:') else t.index(':') + 1
    return [run(t[:i], b=True), run(t[i:])]

sz = lambda n: f'<w:sz w:val="{n}"/><w:szCs w:val="{n}"/>'
P = []
P.append(para([run('BAIR Research Approval Decision', True, sz(23))], 60, 30, 'center'))
P.append(para([run('Pelvic Floor Dysfunction Screening in Female Athletes', True, sz(21))], 0, 200, 'center'))
P.append(para([run('September 29, 2026')], 0, 120))
for i, t in enumerate(['Dr. Laurel Proulx', 'Baylor Pelvic Health and Rehabilitation Research Lab', 'Baylor University']):
    P.append(para([run(t)], 0, 0 if i < 2 else 80))
P.append(para([run('cc: Dr. Mandy Parra, Tarleton State University')], 0, 120))
P.append(para([run(get('Re:'), True)], 0, 120))
P.append(para([run('Dear Dr. Proulx,')]))
P.append(para([run(get('The BAIR Steering Committee has completed'))]))
P.append(para([run('Decision: ', True), run('APPROVED WITH CONDITIONS.', True, GREEN), run(' Approved subject to the conditions listed below.')], 60, 80))
P.append(para(lead(get('Scope:'))))
P.append(para([run(get('The committee scored'))]))
P.append(para([run(get('The committee also noted'))]))
P.append(para([run('Conditions of Approval', True, sz(21) + '<w:u w:val="single"/>')], 130, 60, 'center'))
intro = get('These concern how')
k = intro.index('Recruitment of Baylor')
P.append(para([run(intro[:k]), run(intro[k:], True)]))
for s in ['Recruitment channel.', 'Athlete preparation.', 'Referral pathway.', 'Incentive raffle.',
          'Data use agreement.', 'Sports in scope and timing.', 'IRB status report.']:
    P.append(para(lead(get(s)), 0, 40, num=3))
P.append(para([run('Liaison and Next Steps', True)], 160, 40))
P.append(para([run(get('Eric Rash will serve'))]))
P.append(para([run(get('A letter of support'))]))
P.append(para([run(get('The committee is glad'))], 0, 160))
P.append(para([run('Sincerely,')], 0, 360))
P.append(para([run('Eric Rash', True)], 0, 0))
P.append(para([run('On behalf of the BAIR Steering Committee')], 0, 0))
P.append(para([run('Baylor Athletics Innovation and Research')], 0, 0))

tpl = D + "2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Eval_Report_Phase1.docx"
out = D + "2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Decision_Letter_Phase1.docx"
tmp = out + ".tmp"
with zipfile.ZipFile(tpl) as zi, zipfile.ZipFile(tmp, 'w', zipfile.ZIP_DEFLATED) as zo:
    for it in zi.infolist():
        data = zi.read(it.filename)
        if it.filename == 'word/document.xml':
            x = data.decode('utf8')
            s = x.index('<w:body>') + len('<w:body>'); e = x.index('<w:sectPr')
            x = x[:s] + ''.join(P) + x[e:]
            data = x.encode('utf8')
        zo.writestr(it, data)
os.replace(tmp, out)
print('ok')
EOF

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |
| `reference_baylor-house-style.md` | `baylor-house-style` |
| `feedback_project_idea_capture.md` | `project-idea-capture` |

Note the last row: strip only the **leading** token. `feedback_project_idea_capture.md`
is a feedback memory *about* project-idea capture — its name keeps the word `project`.

`[[links]]` target this bare name, never the filename and never a prefixed variant.

This rule exists because it was previously unwritten: an audit on 2026-09-02 found the
corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in
isolation, so without a stated rule the split regrows on every write.

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

# Closeout

One command that replaces the manual end-of-day sequence: "any loose ends?" → "commit and push what needs to be" → "is this in memory?" → "write a handoff so Codex can pick this up."

Run all five checks, then give ONE verdict. Do not ask permission between steps — the invocation of this skill IS the authorization for the full sequence. Commit and push is standing-authorized for every DEV repo: each repo's `AGENTS.md` Session routine says "update STATUS, commit, push at end", and unpushed work on one machine is the top cause of conflicts on the other. The only exceptions are repos whose `CLAUDE.md` says their data must stay local (DexaProject is the precedent); commit those locally and list them as open.

This one file serves Claude Code, Codex and Cowork (uploaded to claude.ai). Cowork has no TaskList and no Claude Code memory hooks: do what applies there and say what was skipped.

## Step 1 — Loose-ends sweep

- `git status` across **every** repo in DEV, not only the ones named in this conversation. Another session, another harness, or the other machine may have left work dirty, and a closeout that only checks what it remembers touching will say "clear to sign off" over someone else's uncommitted work. Walk `DEV/`, `DEV/Football/` and `DEV/SpecialRequests/`, and report any repo with uncommitted or unpushed commits. The full walk takes about 90 seconds.
  - Windows: `git -C <repo> status --porcelain` per repo. Do NOT use `Get-ChildItem -Recurse` to look for files; it silently skips paths past the 260-character limit. Inside a repo, `git ls-files` is the reliable way to ask whether a file exists.
  - Repos with dirty state you did not touch: commit and push them like any other, and name them in the report so the user knows another session left them.
- Unfinished todos/tasks from this session (TaskList if available).
- Background jobs or workflows still running.
- Anything the user was promised earlier in the session that wasn't delivered.

## Step 2 — Commit & push

- Every repo touched this session: stage, commit with a descriptive message, `git pull --no-rebase` (the other machine may have pushed), push. If the merge conflicts, follow the conflict steps in `dev-sync/SKILL.md` (they are the one home for them), then push and list the file under "Still open".
- Before staging, make sure any new file over 95 MB and any `.env` is in `.gitignore`.
- Local-only repos (CLAUDE.md says so): commit, do not push, list it.
- Also check the three config repos, `~/.claude` (dotclaude), `~/.claude/skills` (claude-skills) and `~/.claude/global-memory` (claude-global-memory). If any has changes, commit and push it the same way, so the other machine's `/dev-sync` picks it up.
- **Push `global-memory` even on a light session.** `daily-backup` pushes it nightly, which is too late for a same-day handoff: work the Mac in the afternoon, sit down at Windows that evening, and anything written to MEMORY.md or handoffs is still only on the Mac. Pushing it here is what makes memory available to the other machine tonight rather than tomorrow. It is the only repo that carries memory across, so treat an unpushed `global-memory` the same as an unpushed project repo: it blocks "clear to sign off".
- Nothing to commit → say so in one line, move on.

## Step 3 — Memory verification

- Check `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/.errors.log` — must be empty. If not, surface contents and fix the hook issue if obvious.
- Confirm today's transcript file exists at `~/.claude/global-memory/transcripts/<today>.md` and was modified within the last few hours. On a Cowork-only day it may be absent; say so, it is not an error.
- Run the dev-docs harvest so repo docs reach memsearch: `bash ~/.claude/scripts/harvest-dev-docs.sh` (Mac) or `powershell -ExecutionPolicy Bypass -File $HOME\.claude\scripts\harvest-dev-docs.ps1` (Windows). Global memory and the repo both cross; Tier A does not. So for every Tier A fact written this session, ask: is this durable and project-scoped? If yes, it must also land in the repo — `docs/STATUS.md` for current state, `docs/DECISIONS.md` for a decision and its reasoning, the dated handoff for the detail. Treat Tier A as a fast local cache and the repo as the record. If a fact only ever exists in Tier A, assume the other machine will never see it.

This is the **canonical durable handoff** — the one future sessions and other harnesses read. (For a mid-session, chat-only summary before `/clear`, that's the `session-handoff` skill; the mattpocock `handoff` skill writes to the OS temp dir and is not durable — don't rely on it for cross-session state.)

If real work happened this session (not just Q&A), write a handoff to
`<repo>/docs/handoffs/<YYYY-MM-DD>-<slug>.md` (or `~/.claude/global-memory/handoffs/` if no repo fits):

- What was being worked on and why
- Decisions made (with the reasoning that would be lost)

```

**Committed & pushed:** <repos + one-line summary, or "nothing to commit">
**STATUS.md:** updated in <repos>
```

# Handoff: Proulx pelvic floor study, Phase 1-only BAIR approval (2026-09-29)

## What and why
Dr. Laurel Proulx's study (Baylor IRB #2373733, pelvic floor dysfunction in female athletes) was approved by BAIR on 2026-08-20. She only wants to use Baylor for Phase 1, the online survey. We updated the decision letter and the evaluation report to say that. Eric emailed both to her on 2026-09-29.

## Decisions
- **Scope.** Baylor participation is Phase 1 only. Baylor athletes are not recruited into Phase 2, and the survey version sent to Baylor athletes must not include the Phase 2 opt-in. Any future Phase 2 use of Baylor athletes needs a new request to the committee.
- **Score unchanged.** It stays at 75/100 (High Priority). The scope change is framed as her clarification after the review, not a rescore.
- **Condition 5 narrowed.** It used to cover Phase 2 collection on Tarleton equipment. It now covers only Tarleton's access to Baylor athletes' Phase 1 survey data. She can close it by confirming in writing that Tarleton won't access that data. The numbering and the "items 1 through 5" gating are unchanged.
- **Terminology.** "Sports Medicine" became "Athletic Medicine" and "strength and conditioning staff" became "Athletic Performance staff."
- **Styling.** The letter was rebuilt in the eval report's style (BU logo header, gold rule, Aptos, green decision label). This is now the standing style for BAIR letters and reports.

## Files
Folder: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\04_RESEARCH\02_Proposals\Approved\2026-08-20_Proulx_PelvicFloor_FemaleAthletes\`
- `2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Decision_Letter_Phase1.docx` and `.pdf` (sent)
- `2026-09-29_Proulx_PFD_Eval_Report_Phase1.docx` and `.pdf` (sent)
- The originals (8/20 and 8/27 versions) were left unchanged.

Template script: `G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\04_RESEARCH\02_Proposals\_templates\build_bair_decision_letter.py`. It rebuilds a letter by putting new body content into the report .docx.

Tier A memory, Windows slug for the Proulx folder:
- `feedback_bair-document-styling.md`
- `project_proulx-approval-status.md`
- `MEMORY.md`

## Next actions (Eric)
1. Agree the recruitment channel with her in writing (condition 1). It can't go through coaches or Athletic Performance staff.
2. Connect her with Athletic Medicine for athlete preparation and the referral contact (conditions 2–3).
3. Send the $50 gift card raffle to NCAA compliance (condition 4).

## Waiting on Proulx
- The Tarleton data use agreement, or written confirmation that Tarleton won't access Baylor athlete data (condition 5).
- The list of Baylor sports in scope (condition 6).
- Her IRB status report, due 2026-10-30. The committee should be copied.
